line: Did you know, the Rolling Stones played their first ever gig on Oxford Street?
fact: On 12 July 1962 the Rolling Stones played their first live show at the Marquee Club, then in a basement under a cinema on Oxford Street. The club moved to Wardour Street in 1964.

line: Did you know, the Ziggy Stardust album cover was shot in a little street off Regent Street?
fact: In January 1972 David Bowie posed outside number 23 Heddon Street for the cover of Ziggy Stardust. Fans still photograph themselves on the doorstep, and a plaque now marks the spot.
source: Wikipedia: The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars

line: Did you know, the Hatton Garden burglars got into the vault down a lift shaft?
fact: Over the Easter weekend of 2015, a gang climbed down a lift shaft into a Hatton Garden safe deposit vault and drilled through its wall with an industrial drill. They took up to £14 million.
source: Wikipedia: Hatton Garden safe deposit burglary

line: Did you know, Edgar Allan Poe went to school in Stoke Newington?
fact: The American writer Edgar Allan Poe was a pupil at the Manor House School on Church Street, Stoke Newington, around 1818, while his foster parents were living in Britain.
source: Wikipedia: Edgar Allan Poe; Stoke Newington

line: Did you know, one of the biggest robberies in history happened in a Knightsbridge side street?
fact: In July 1987 two men entered a safe deposit centre in Cheval Place asking to rent a box. They left with about £60 million, one of the largest robberies in history.

line: Did you know, the blue door from the film Notting Hill belonged to the man who wrote it?
fact: Hugh Grant's house in the 1999 film Notting Hill is 280 Westbourne Park Road, owned by the film's writer, Richard Curtis. The blue door was auctioned for charity; today's door is blue again.

line: Did you know, Brixton's Electric Avenue was the first market street lit by electricity?
fact: Electric Avenue in Brixton was the first market street to be lit by electricity. Eddy Grant's 1982 hit song Electric Avenue is named after it.

line: Did you know, the playwright Christopher Marlowe lies in an unmarked grave in Deptford?
fact: Christopher Marlowe, one of the most famous Elizabethan playwrights, was killed in a house in Deptford in 1593. He was buried in an unmarked grave in St Nicholas's churchyard.

line: Did you know, robbers near Heathrow came for £1 million in cash and found three tonnes of gold?
fact: In November 1983 six robbers broke into a warehouse by Heathrow expecting about £1 million in Spanish money. They found three tonnes of gold instead, worth £26 million. Most of it was never recovered.

line: Did you know, Ealing has the oldest working film studio in the world?
fact: Ealing Studios is the oldest continuously working film studio in the world. Films have been made on the site since 1902.
